title: U.S. House · Washington's 5th District
area: Eastern Washington, including Spokane and the surrounding region.

context.text: Michael Baumgartner and Carmela Conroy advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary out of a field of twelve candidates.

candidates.name: Michael Baumgartner
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary

summary.text: Michael Baumgartner is the Republican incumbent in Washington's 5th District, elected in 2024 to succeed Cathy McMorris Rodgers. A Pullman native with an economics degree from Washington State University and a Harvard master's in public administration, he worked as a State Department officer in Baghdad before serving eight years in the Washington State Senate and six years as Spokane County Treasurer.

background.text: Born in Pullman, Washington, in 1975. According to his campaign website, he grew up among the Palouse wheat fields in Colton and then Pullman, the son of two educators.

Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Washington State University (1999) and a Master's of Public Administration in international development from Harvard University (2002). His campaign website says he spent a year volunteering with the Jesuits in Africa before Harvard, where he was a Teaching Fellow in Economics.

After working in private business in the Middle East, served as a U.S. State Department officer at the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Iraq, from 2007 to 2008, then as a counternarcotics advisor to a U.S. government-funded program in Afghanistan; also worked as a part-time economic adviser to the U.S. military.
Was the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Washington in 2012, according to his campaign website.

Served in the Washington State Senate representing the 6th Legislative District from 2011 to 2019. His campaign website says he played a lead role in creating a WSU medical school in Spokane, in funding the North-South Freeway, and in a reduction in college tuition, and that his "Drain the Swamp" legislation eliminated five state agencies.
Served as Spokane County Treasurer from 2019 to 2025, overseeing a roughly $1.9 billion fixed-income investment fund.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2024 and took office in 2025. Serves on the Judiciary, Foreign Affairs, and Education and the Workforce committees; his official site lists him as vice chair of the Education and the Workforce Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development, chairman of the College Sports Caucus, and vice chair of the Republican Policy Committee.
His official biography lists honors including the Washington Policy Center's "Champion of Freedom Award" and the Inland Empire Society of American Foresters' "Legislator of the Year" award.
Lives in Spokane with his wife, Eleanor, and their five children, according to his official biography.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Courts, Intellectual Property, AI and the Internet subcommittee; Administrative State, Regulatory Reform and Antitrust subcommittee), the Committee on Education and the Workforce, and the Committee on Foreign Affairs for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Served in the Washington State Senate representing the 6th Legislative District from 2011 to 2019.

candidates.name: Carmela Conroy
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary

summary.text: Carmela Conroy is a Democrat and a Spokane native who worked as a Spokane County deputy prosecutor before a 24-year career as a U.S. Foreign Service officer. She won the 2024 top-two primary for this seat and lost the general election to Michael Baumgartner, and she is running again on lowering costs, protecting Medicare and Medicaid, and ending tariffs.

background.text: Born in Spokane, Washington, and graduated from Central Valley High School. Describes herself as a third-generation Eastern Washingtonian whose grandfather was a union mason on the Grand Coulee Dam and whose father was a railroad worker.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Washington, a law degree from the University of Washington School of Law, and a graduate degree from the U.S. Naval War College in 2004. Her campaign says she worked her way through school.
Returned to Spokane after law school as a Spokane County deputy prosecutor for four years, working on cases involving survivors of violence and sexual assault, according to her campaign.

Served about 24 years as a U.S. Foreign Service officer, with postings listed on her campaign website as Afghanistan, Japan, New Zealand, Norway, Pakistan, and Washington, D.C. Her campaign says she negotiated access to foreign ports for U.S. Navy ships, bilateral trade agreements, and militia disarmament.
Her campaign website says she received national recognition during her service, including one of the CIA's highest civilian awards.
Ran for this seat in 2024: advanced from the August top-two primary and lost the November 5 general election to Michael Baumgartner, who won 60.6%.
Has been affiliated with the League of Women Voters, Friends of the Bluff, Spokane Preservation Advocates, and the American Foreign Service Association.

priorities.text: Calls for ending "tariff chaos" to lower prices for consumers and businesses and restore normal trade relations with Canada and Mexico.
Supports restoring Medicare and Medicaid funding, extending Medicaid coverage to all children up to age 19, and allowing federal health programs to negotiate lower drug prices.
Calls for a federal minimum-wage law indexed to inflation with paid time off and paid sick leave.
On government accountability, supports prohibiting members of Congress from trading individual stocks.

positions.summary: Calls for ending current tariff policy, saying it would cut prices for consumers and businesses and restore normal trade relations with neighboring countries.
Supports restoring Medicare and Medicaid funding to previous levels, extending Medicaid to all children under 19, and allowing federal health programs to negotiate drug prices.
Supports an inflation-indexed federal minimum wage with paid time off and paid sick leave.
Calls for defunding border-security assets not directed to official ports of entry and defunding detention-center construction, while excepting people facing criminal charges.
